change: Materialize the aux owner's committed logits_positions directly at seal after trimming; retain per-append continuity checks, observed position_ids, CUDA fences and publication validation.
limitations: Single H100, Qwen3-0.6B BF16, local TCP Store and HTTP test Catalog; no new distributed or RDMA coverage.
One ordinary off/on/off round per source, followed by candidate-first diagnostic rounds with scheduler GC logging. Logging changes the environment; these are not pooled as equivalent repetitions.

The ordinary candidate throughput and p99 TTFT regress. Diagnostic reversal does not reproduce the large spike but still has higher candidate TTFT and mixed raw/off-normalized throughput. End-to-end speedup is not established.
CPU trace operator events include nested dispatch; counts are not allocation counts, durations are inclusive and cannot be summed as wall time.
Position materialization at seal is outside teacher-append profiling scopes; scope time reduction is not total request or service latency reduction.
Profile driver verifies publication counts but does not read tensors back. Separate runtime and serving suites provide numerical/contract checks.

Long diagnostic scheduler GC events precede the client's model_info request; no attribution of the original in-flight spike is proven. Client/tokenizer GC is not instrumented and request records lack a wall-clock anchor.
Serving uses a GPFS journal; profiler uses a node-local journal. Startup, warmup, drain and readback are excluded from request timing.
Production SLO, production Catalog retention, SpecForge checkpoint integration and trained draft quality remain open.
